score.band_label: Skeleton — the right structure with almost nothing in it. The slot contract, the class taxonomy, the clip census, the impact and material model and the seam crossing are genuinely built and genuinely driven; the animation they describe is never drawn, and the reach the fingerprint measures is up to 1.90 m longer than the reach that can touch a body.

biggest_gap.what: The moveset animation model — 1150 distinct clips over 2689 slots and 87 weapons, the solved arcs, the solved blade lengths, the 25-slot contract — has no renderer. `grep -rn "weapon" game/src/render/` returns nothing, `grep -rn "bone" game/src/render/` returns nothing, and no SkinnedMesh is constructed anywhere in game/src. `game/src/render/scene.js` makeActor() builds a rigid group of nine primitives — torso, head, snout, hips, two static legs, two static arms — plus `new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.055, 0.95, 0.014)` welded at local (0.40, 1.28, 0.10) as 'the blade', one 0.95 m box for all eighty-seven weapons. `game/src/render/renderer.js:398-399` is the whole of the player's animation: playerMesh.position.set(sim.player.pos) and playerMesh.rotation.y = yaw. Measured in the shipping build: across a full 60-frame r1.1, the character-box pixel change is 0.19% peak for hlb_garrison_bill (2.85 m, a 146.8 deg sweep over 14 active frames) and 0.21% for cgs_drowned_reaper (a `spin` over 18 active frames); ssw_garrison_sword's 2.4% is flat from f030 to f060 and is the root lunge translating a rigid mesh, not a swing. Frame-0 screenshots of ssw_garrison_sword (1.95 m), hlb_garrison_bill (2.85 m) and cgs_drowned_reaper (2.75 m) are byte-identical, md5 9bdb823fbcdb3ba820b2946b05ffa55a.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: WEAPON-CRITIC 0 states this role's whole subject: 'the deficit lives entirely in the animation-clip column of the moveset data and in the root tracks the clips produce.' ARBITRATION 3's CONSUMPTION check states the consequence: 'a model with no demonstrated consumer is unmeasurable => 0, exactly as a missing model is — from the player's chair they are the same thing', and it lists 'character creation rendered 20 byte-identical screenshots while returning correct values' as one of the four wave-1 instances. This is that instance again, in the area the check was written for. Round 1 found the 87 movesets unreachable from the running game; round 3 made them reachable to the hitbox solver; they are still unreachable to the screen. The builder demonstrated a consumer for the IMPACT model, correctly and convincingly, and never asked the same question of the ANIMATION model — whose only consumer is the solver that grades it. It is also the mechanism by which every other defect here survived three rounds: the blade points 35-52 degrees into the ground and sits 100% below the floor plane through the entire damaging window of CGS, HLB, TSW and WHP (so a halberd lands nothing at 2.65 m and nothing at all against a retreating target), and that is invisible to a critic who cannot see the swing and unmissable to anyone who can. The builder named the blade inclination as its own biggest remaining defect; this is the reason it was still there to name.

remedy.action: Pose the rendered actor from the transforms the simulation already computes every frame. CombatBody.rig produces socketA/socketB and a full bone dump and engine.getHitGeometry() already returns both in world space, so nothing new has to be computed — makeActor() must expose its arm and weapon nodes, and the per-frame update must write those nodes' positions and orientations from combat.bodyOf('player') (and from each enemy body) instead of writing only the group's position and yaw. Scale the weapon mesh from the moveset's socket_b distance so a 3.6 m whip is not a 0.95 m box.

secondary_observations.what: CR_mean = 0.4219 in reports/W1-10-connect-rate.json is deflated by an instrument bug and should not be quoted. tools/weapons/connect-rate.mjs increments its `presses` denominator on every re-seat inside a loop that runs `gap*PRESSES + 200` frames, so it books 12 presses for 10 scripted ones whenever gap ~ 100. Every healthy axe, sword and mace reads exactly 10/12 = 0.833 with hits_at_reach = 10 — ten hits from ten presses, scored 0.833. The zeros are unaffected and are real: HLB 6/6, TSW 5/5 and WHP 4/4 land nothing at their own declared reach minus 0.20 m. But `weapons_landing_nothing` is empty and CR_band averages 0.828, so 'a weapon class that connects zero percent of the time' is too strong: the long classes connect only at short-weapon distances, which is a different and equally serious defect.

The builder's own runtime blind pack reports three defects nobody asked it to: the weapon tip is below the floor plane on 13%-68% of every trace's frames and reaches -2.83 m; peak tip speeds of 200.9, 189.5, 160.3, 144.7 and 137.5 m/s appear against RI-WPN05 E's widest band ceiling of 40 m/s; and 2 to 4 hits land per 20-second trace from 8 to 40 swings. A blind pack that surfaces its own build's worst problems without being asked is the best instrument in this piece and should be kept unchanged.

'Two shipping crashes fixed' is one and a half. At 6e359ab `advanceAlong` had three call sites in game/src/combat/system.js and no definition, and `bodyDamage` had one reference in game/src/combat/resolve.js and no definition — four sites, and both would have thrown out of CombatSystem.step. Both are defined exactly once now and the fix is real. But the builder's own status file records that `bodyDamage` was supplied by a concurrent W1-09-r4 agent and that its own duplicate definition was removed after an 'Identifier already declared' error. The finding is the builder's; half the fix is not.

reports/w1-10-blind-r3/PACK-SUMMARY.json publishes tip_radius_max_m and tip_speed_max_mps per trace. Those are D5 and RI-WPN05 E's headline in summary form and they make the M6 grouping decidable without opening a trace. The per-trace JSON files are clean; the summary should not be handed to a blind judge.

tools/weapons/impact-consumption.mjs and the round-2 kritik-consumption3.mjs both write game/data/weapons/classes.json on disk and restore it in a finally. In a tree thirteen agents share that is one crash from leaving a corrupted tracked data file and one concurrent `git commit -a` from banking it — which is exactly how HEAD acquired a reverted socketsFor this round, per the builder's own URGENT status note. Perturbation probes should mutate an in-memory copy; kritik3-consumption.mjs shows it is no harder.

gap_closure.acceptance_restated: The round-2 acceptance ('kritik-consumption3.mjs reports 6 of 6 CONSUMED') is NOT met and should not have been written that way: four of its six probes perturb rows a flesh dummy cannot read or observe quantities its vector does not record. Restated acceptance, met: every load-bearing row of the RI-WPN05 A/B tables, driven against a fixture that can express it, changes a BEHAVIOURAL quantity (damage dealt, frames the animation actually stalled, body displacement, real move length) and not merely a field of the impact record; and the suite contains at least one probe a correct build leaves INERT.
gap_closure.note: Adjudicating 17/17 against 2/6. AMENDMENT-W1-10-03 E is UPHELD and its VOID-not-INERT rule is ADOPTED, with two corrections. Against the round-2 critic: its 2/6 was one probe too pessimistic — `knockback_m ALL -> 9` IS consumed on its own flesh fixture (it moves the victim 9 m) and was missed only because the observation vector was {dmg, hitF, attacker hitstop}; my run of the unmodified round-2 rows scores 3/6. Against the builder: 17/17 is one cell too optimistic — `hitstop.victim_delta.flesh 4 -> 60` moved only the impact RECORD against a passive dummy that has no animation clock to stall; driven against inf_trash mid-attack the victim's animation holds 16 -> 72 frames, so the row is genuinely consumed but the probe that demonstrated it was not the probe that could. Right conclusion, one wrong cell. I add one clause to E: a CONSUMPTION suite must also carry at least one probe a correct build leaves INERT, or '17/17 CONSUMED' is indistinguishable from an instrument that fires on everything.

arbitration_questions.question: Does the CONSUMPTION check in ARBITRATION 3 require a RENDERED consumer, or is a simulation-side consumer sufficient? The wave-1 examples it cites are split: 'character creation rendered 20 byte-identical screenshots while returning correct values' is a rendering failure, while '50 of 55 magic effects were a single generic applicator' and 'the stealth visibility term was computed every frame while the alert meter never read it' are simulation failures. W1-10's animation model has a simulation consumer (the hitbox solver) and no rendered consumer, and the answer decides whether this piece's biggest gap is in remit for critic.weapons or belongs to critic.ui. I have scored it in remit, on the ground that WEAPON-CRITIC 2's out-of-remit list does not exclude it and that ARBITRATION 3's own words are 'from the player's chair they are the same thing', but the ruling should be written down rather than inferred.

RI-WPN02 B defines Reach (m) as a horizontal radius with root translation suppressed and says nothing about the blade's height. The shipping build satisfies it on 85 of 87 weapons while four classes swing entirely below the floor plane. Should the definition be replaced with usable reach — the furthest point on the damaging capsule inside a standing target's torso band — as proposed in this verdict's bar_pressure? That changes D5, and therefore D_min, Dg_min, SEP, W_min and W_med, for every build measured so far.

self_audit.self_audit_note: ran_every_assigned_method is FALSE. Recorded rather than skipped, each as a check with result 'unmeasurable' scored 0 fail-closed per CRITIC-DOCTRINE 7.3: RI-WPN04 M5 (situational superiority, unrun for a third round, blocked on the same missing archetype dummies); RI-WPN07 M1-M5 (RVS, blocked on 8 missing archetypes, an absent policy file and an unimplemented H.runPolicy — the instrument was WRITTEN and exits non-zero naming each blocker); RI-WPN02 M5b (the new heavy-shape check); RI-WPN03 M2b and D.3 Chg; and RI-WPN05 F ILS was reported from the builder's figures with its bar defect adjudicated rather than re-derived. Ladder rungs used, in order: (1) recomputed all the headline numbers with my own instruments — D_min, Dg_min, SEP, W_min, W_med, ARI, CFS, TDV — and found the builder's arithmetic sound, with my own D11 error found and corrected against it; (2) changed the sample per WEAPON-CRITIC 8's known good rung, to the classes with the longest declared reach rather than the ones the probes demo, which is where the blade-attitude defect is; (3) stopped trusting the observed column and asked whether it is a measurement at all, by perturbing the animation and the declaration separately — which is where the setpoint finding is; (4) applied the new protocol rule and made the target move, which is where the retreating-target zero is; (5) looked at the pixels, which is where the biggest gap is. No builder tool produced a number in this verdict; tools/weapons/fingerprint.mjs, deletion-test.mjs, blind-pack.mjs and impact-consumption.mjs were read to be audited and never executed to produce a score. The blind pack itself is builder-generated and is used as an artifact rather than as an instrument: its trace rows were inspected for design-column leakage and the picks were derived from the motion columns by my own feature extraction.

notes: Prose verdict: corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/W1-10-r3.md. Three things this round did that should be said plainly and are easy to lose under a 3/10. (1) The builder found and published a trade in which a PASSING SEP (1.4605) was given up for arc conformance (21.1% -> 7.59% of 606 clips outside tolerance) and reported the resulting FAILING 1.3858 with both builds' numbers on the record. I verified the account and it holds; that is exactly the behaviour this project wants. The qualification is in the .md 1: the earlier passing number was itself a readback of the declaration, so what was traded was not a measurement. (2) The round-2 biggest gap is genuinely closed, on my instrument and not the builder's, and AMENDMENT-W1-10-03 E's VOID-not-INERT rule is upheld and adopted with one clause added. (3) tools/weapons/deletion-test.mjs finding that its own first version could not fail — a cache-busting import busts one module and leaves transitive imports cached, so three cases reported 'no change' because the deletion never landed — is the single most creditable thing in the round, and it is the AGENT-PROTOCOL failure mode 2 caught by the agent that would have benefited from not catching it.
